title: Multi-use recreation facility prioritized in capital plan
subtitle: Draft 2026 capital budget, water meter contract, Connecting Links grant, election signs, battery storage agreement and tourism strategy
overview: Council voted to prioritize a multi-use recreation facility in the draft 2026 Ten Year Capital Forecast {{vote:m9}}. Staff said debt capacity and development charges do not allow both this facility and a new ice pad at the same time. A proposed amendment that would have added future ice pad capacity was not accepted as friendly, and no vote was recorded on it. Council also received the facility feasibility study and business plan and sent them to three advisory committees {{vote:m7}}.

Council directed staff to include the 2026 preliminary draft capital budget in the staff draft budget {{vote:m2}}. It awarded the water meter replacement contract {{vote:m3}} and approved a Connecting Links grant application for repaving Tower and Bridge Streets in Fergus {{vote:m4}}.

Council also authorized a new election sign by-law {{vote:m5}}, which was later passed. It approved a community benefit agreement with the Elora battery storage project and an allocation policy for the funds {{vote:m6}}. Staff will bring the final economic development and tourism strategy back on October 27, 2025 {{vote:m10}}.

decisions.detail: Council prioritized construction of a multi-use recreation facility in the draft 2026 Ten Year Capital Forecast {{vote:m9}}.
Staff were directed to include the 2026 Preliminary Draft Capital Budget in the 2026 Staff Draft Budget {{vote:m2}}.
The contract was awarded to Neptune Technology Group Canada Co at an upset limit of $2,838,901 for supply and installation of 4720 meters, with funding revised {{vote:m3}}.
Staff will apply for Connecting Links funding to repave Tower and Bridge Streets in Fergus, with an estimated $130,000 township share from the General Capital Reserve if successful {{vote:m4}}.
Council received the feasibility study and business plan for information and sent them to ConnectCW and three advisory committees {{vote:m7}}.
Council received the draft strategy for information and directed staff to gather feedback and return with a final report on October 27, 2025 {{vote:m10}}.

debate: Delegates from soccer, rugby and basketball groups said the township lacks indoor turf, a walking track and a full gymnasium. They said current gyms are full, and a facility could support partnerships and tournament tourism.
A resident delegate argued council should not have to choose between the two projects. The delegate asked why costs were so high and urged a simpler approach within existing funds.

Staff said debt servicing limits and uncertain development charge cash flow make doing both projects at once impractical. They said the choice sets the order in the budget book. One councillor's proposal to add future ice pad capacity was not treated as a friendly amendment and was set aside for a simpler motion.

On the ERP software, one councillor questioned whether the HR package was needed for the township's size. Staff replied that existing financial systems are reaching end of life and that recruitment is currently handled manually.

On the economic strategy, councillors said agri-tourism and sport tourism were under-represented. Consultants cited limited consumer-facing farms and a shortage of accommodation, and council noted the strategy can be revised before final approval.
